judged_text: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null (the assignment on lines 1063-1067 explicitly produces null when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination), silently discarding every collected member destination calendar. A COLLECTIVE booking whose organizer has no destination calendar but whose team members do never creates events on the members' calendars — the exact multi-host scenario this PR claims to fix — with no error logged anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is explicitly set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, in the COLLECTIVE branch, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which becomes a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, silently discarding the collected team member destination calendars. This is directly verifiable from the diff and breaks the intended multi-destination behavior for the edge case where only non-organizer hosts have destination calendars.
